title: Recombination Landscape of Chromosome 7
desc: Crossover density along chromosome 7 wound into a single ideogram; chords mark long-range linkage disequilibrium blocks that survive across 3,041 genomes.

comments.txt: The chord weighting reads beautifully — is that LD r²?
It is — thresholded at 0.6 to keep it legible.

title: The Weight of a Single p-Value
desc: A height GWAS across twelve chromosomes. The dashed line is genome-wide significance; everything above it earned the right to be called a locus.

comments.txt: That one spike on chr4 is doing a lot of work.
Framed this for the lab wall.
-log10(p) has never looked so calm.

title: Cortical Cell Atlas, Layer V
desc: 126,400 single nuclei from motor cortex, embedded. Each cloud is a transcriptional identity; the space between them is everything we still call "transitional".

comments.txt: The isolation of that top cluster is striking.

title: Mycelial Concordance
desc: A concordance tree of 214 fungal isolates. The green clade is the one that refused to move no matter which gene we rooted on.

comments.txt: Concordance factors as colour — clever.

title: Tumor Microenvironment No. 3
desc: Spatial neighborhoods from imaging mass cytometry, tessellated. Each cell is coloured by its dominant niche; the walls are where two ecologies meet.

comments.txt: Colours map to niche, not cell type — a common question.
This is the best a Voronoi has ever looked.

title: Interactome at First Light
desc: A yeast protein–protein interaction subnetwork, communities recovered by Leiden clustering. Hubs sized by degree; you can find the proteasome by eye.

title: Expression, Clustered (n = 384)
desc: Bulk RNA-seq across a differentiation time-course, rows and columns reordered by hierarchical clustering. The dendrogram remembers the order the biology chose.

comments.txt: Row-scaled z-scores? The banding is gorgeous.

title: Isoforms of the Deep
desc: A long-read isoform density surface for a single gene locus, rendered as a relief map. Each contour is a splice junction the polymerase kept choosing.

comments.txt: Reading exon usage as topography — I love this.

title: Fold No. 12 — Large Subunit
desc: A predicted ribbon trace of a ribosomal protein, warm-lit. Structure is the one figure in biology that was always meant to be sculpture.

comments.txt: The lighting sells the depth.
pLDDT gradient would be a nice variant.

title: Synteny Between Two Grasses
desc: Collinear blocks between two grass genomes drawn as ribbons across a shared wheel. Whole-genome duplication, thirty million years on, still legible.

comments.txt: You can see the ancient tetraploidy right there.

title: Stipple Study: Drift
desc: A flow field seeded with nothing but noise, stippled the way the ART in our own wordmark is built. No data — just the grammar of a scatter plot, pushed.

comments.txt: The density falloff at the edges is so satisfying.

title: Voronoi Nocturne
desc: The same tessellation that maps cell neighborhoods, run at night with a cold palette and no biology attached. A tool remembering it can also just be beautiful.

comments.txt: Nocturne is right. This is calm.

title: Phylogeny of Nothing in Particular
desc: A tree inferred from randomly generated sequences. It means nothing, and it branches anyway — which is either a warning about our methods or a small poem.

comments.txt: "branches anyway" — ha. Bootstrap this? 😄

title: Contours for a Fictional Genome
desc: A coverage track for a genome that does not exist, rendered as a warm relief. Every peak is a read depth we simply decided to believe in.

comments.txt: No repo? I need this method.
Cleaning it up — repo soon.

title: Circos, Unbound
desc: Circos with no genome to answer to — just arcs, links and the pleasure of closing a plot into a circle. Green because spring.

comments.txt: circlize is criminally underused for art.

title: Latent Bloom
desc: A UMAP of pure Gaussian blobs, shaded by density. The embedding finds structure that was never there — which is, of course, the whole anxiety of the method.

comments.txt: The honest version of every embedding figure.

title: Field Notes (Vector)
desc: Particles walked through a vector field in indigo and brass, the colours of the emblem. A quiet study in how little you need for motion to read on a still page.
